title: Muse Glimmer: a 30B Open-Weight Model Built for Always-On Local Agents
hook: Meta released a 30B dense multimodal model under Apache 2.0, tuned for agents that run all day on your own machine — quantized to ~4-bit it fits under 20 GB.
key_points: 30B dense parameters, released as open weights under a permissive Apache 2.0 license.
Multimodal: interleaved text and images through a dedicated perception encoder.
Trained on 100+ languages, with controllable reasoning effort to trade quality against speed.
Full precision needs 55+ GB; ~4-bit quantization brings the language model under 20 GB, leaving headroom on a 24 GB card.
Positioned for always-on local agent workflows rather than one-off chat.
content_html: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight model aimed squarely at agents that run continuously on your own hardware rather than at a chat window.
extra_html:
What shipped

Muse Glimmer is a dense 30B model released under Apache 2.0. It takes interleaved text and images through a dedicated perception encoder, was trained across more than 100 languages, and exposes a controllable reasoning-effort setting so callers can trade answer quality against latency. Meta puts the full-precision memory footprint at 55+ GB, which rules out consumer cards; quantizing the weights to roughly 4 bits brings the language model under 20 GB and leaves headroom inside a 24 GB GPU.

Why it matters

Most open-weight releases are framed around benchmark scores. This one is framed around a deployment envelope: a model small enough and cheap enough to leave running all day, doing agent work locally, with the vision stack included rather than bolted on. That combination — permissive license, multimodal input, and a memory budget that a single consumer GPU can actually hold — is what makes always-on local agents plausible outside a datacenter.

flashcards.prompt: Why does Muse Glimmer's 4-bit quantization matter for its stated use case?
flashcards.back_html: At full precision the 30B model needs 55+ GB — beyond consumer hardware. Quantized to ~4-bit the language model drops under 20 GB, so it fits on a 24 GB consumer GPU with headroom to spare.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'controllable reasoning effort' buy a local agent?
flashcards.back_html: A quality/speed dial: the same model can think harder on difficult steps or answer fast on cheap ones — useful when an agent runs continuously on limited local hardware.
